rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.2 <U+2014> three-year (2011-2013) split-plot field experiment with four replications at Kruszyn Krajenski, central Poland, factors drip irrigation (O/D) and N fertilization method (broadcasting P / drip fertigation F). Q2: Section 3.2 and Tables 6 and 8 <U+2014> nitrogen fertigation significantly raised mean marketable tuber yield from 28.85 to 32.28 t/ha (about 12%) and tuber number per plant from 10.3 to 12.8 compared with broadcasting; highest yield in the D+F treatment (40.47 t/ha).
rows.notes: The study's own figures match the claimed 11.8% yield and 24.2% tuber-number increases (28.85 to 32.28 t/ha; 10.3 to 12.8 tubers). Q3: one method only (replicated plot harvest). Q4: tuber weight and number are reported as yield components (Tables 7-8, Figure 5), but no mechanistic intermediate for the fertigation effect (nutrient availability, uptake, soil N or soil water data) is measured; the mechanism of higher root density in the wet zone is only cited; answered no with doubt. Q5: one site, one soil, one cultivar; years are not sites. Q6: 11.25 m2 plots only. Q7: the authors note IWUE for D+F was higher in drier years and that heavy 2012 rainfall lowered IWUE, but this is an observed variation, not a stated requirement for the fertigation yield effect. Q8: no limitations of the result are stated. Q9: only Tukey letter groupings and significance asterisks; no SD, SE, CI or range for the fertigation effect.

notes: Full text appears complete, though pages 4-5 and 10 contain duplicated/garbled text from overlapping page layouts (preprint and final versions interleaved); the tables were still readable.
